explanation: Without synchronization, increment operations are not atomic; counter may end up as 0, 1, or 2.
lock ensures only one thread enters critical section; counter increments safely to 2.
Join() waits for thread to complete; A prints first, then B.
Interlocked.Increment performs atomic increment; no race condition, always 2.
WaitOne() blocks until Set() is called; prints Go after signal.
ThreadLocal<T> stores separate values per thread; each thread has its own value.
Mutex exclusive locking prevents race conditions; counter safely increments to 2.
Sleep() pauses thread execution for specified milliseconds.
Circular lock dependency: t1 waits for lock2 while holding lock1, t2 waits for lock1 while holding lock2.
Semaphore(2, 2) allows at most 2 threads to enter; third waits until one releases.
